newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania coffee board steps up marketing.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania coffee board steps up marketing.

text.p: Tanzania is to step up government and private sector promotion of its coffee industry, a senior coffee official said on Thursday.
The country would participate for the first time at a speciality coffee exhibition in the U.S. in April, said Damian Salla, chief spokesman for the state-run Tanzania Coffee Board (TCB).
"To improve our marketing, we will be participating in international events -- an exhibition at New Orleans by the Speciality Coffee Association of America (SCAA)," Salla told Reuters.

"Through such meetings we talk about our coffee and promote it," he said. The New Orleans exhibition will be held from April 18-22 and then the globe-trotting TCB will pack up and move to Japan for the Tokyo International Trade Fair on April 24-25.
"We have the German market which we have to maintain -- it is a good one. But Japan and the U.S. we are developing," Salla said.

Apart from high-profile exhibitions, the TCB said it had allocated a small budget to produce promotional video films about Tanzania's coffee industry and a film is expected to be completed later this year.
Other marketing incentives include organised visits by major coffee traders to Tanzania, sponsored by the industry and TCB, he said.
Tanzania's premium coffee is its mild-washed arabicas grown around the foothills of Mount Kilimanjaro. Smaller quantities of robusta are grown in the south and northwest Kagera region.
Coffee is Tanzania's most important agricultural export earner of foreign exchange, though yields are forecast to decline in 1996/97 because of poor rains.
